verdict.summary: ServiceNow does not have one central OAuth app or review process. Each instance acts as its own authorization server, and an admin on that instance creates the OAuth client in System OAuth > Application Registry. You can get started without waiting for anyone, but every customer's instance admin has to create a client (or approve one) before that customer can connect. ServiceNow only reviews apps listed on the optional ServiceNow Store.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own instance, plus about 15 min of admin work in each customer instance
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 30-60 min (sign up for a free Personal Developer Instance, then register the client)
verdict.approval_wait: none (optional ServiceNow Store certification is reported at 3-5 weeks)

gates.name: Personal Developer Instance (PDI)
gates.unlocks: You connect your own ServiceNow account through your own OAuth client, on a free PDI or on any instance where you have the admin role.
limits: Access tokens last 30 minutes (1800 s) by default, so tokens are refreshed often
Refresh tokens expire after 100 days (8640000 s) by default, after which the user must re-authorize
Rate limits depend on the instance's Rate Limit Rules. Going over them returns HTTP 429

gates.name: Customer instance OAuth client (per instance)
gates.unlocks: Users on a specific customer's instance can connect once that instance's admin creates an OAuth client and gives you the Client ID and Client Secret.
limits: An admin has to act in every customer instance. One client cannot be reused across instances
Each instance's admin controls scopes, token lifespans and rate limits
If the instance uses SSO, the login redirects to that instance's IdP
gates.time_to_reach: About 15 min of admin work in each customer instance, plus however long it takes to coordinate with them

gates.name: Production across any instance / ServiceNow Store (optional)
gates.unlocks: Any ServiceNow customer can connect once their admin registers a client. No ServiceNow approval is needed for OAuth access. Store certification only applies if you distribute a scoped app through the ServiceNow Store.
limits: Store certification includes platform integration, implementation security, performance and license reviews
Store apps may need to be recertified for new releases or versions
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for OAuth access. Store certification is reported at 3-5 weeks

steps.title: Create a ServiceNow developer account and request a PDI
steps.detail: Sign in at developer.servicenow.com (the site needs JavaScript) and click Request Instance. When it's ready, write down the instance URL (for example https://dev12345.service-now.com) and the admin credentials. The subdomain (dev12345) is what Composio uses.
gotchas: You need to sign in to request an instance. The PDI inactivity and reclaim rules were not verified.

steps.title: Create a Composio ServiceNow auth config and copy its callback URL
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the servicenow toolkit using the OAUTH2 scheme. Composio has no managed app for ServiceNow, so you have to supply your own client. Copy the callback URL it shows (the default is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add).

steps.title: Open the Application Registry and start a new OAuth endpoint
steps.detail: Log in to the instance as an admin and go to All > System OAuth > Application Registry, then click New. On releases before Zurich, choose 'Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients'. On Zurich and later, choose New Inbound Integration Experience > New Integration, then pick the authorization code grant option.
gotchas: The UI labels changed in Zurich. Use whichever path matches your release.

steps.title: Fill in the endpoint form and save
steps.detail: Enter a Name, leave Client Secret blank so it is generated for you, check Active, and paste the Composio callback into Redirect URL exactly as shown. You can keep the default Access Token Lifespan (1800 s) and Refresh Token Lifespan (8640000 s). Save the record, then copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: If the URL doesn't match, authorization fails with 'Invalid Redirect_URI'.
It is unverified whether the field accepts multiple comma-separated URLs.

steps.title: Enter credentials and instance subdomain in Composio
steps.detail: Add the Client ID, Client Secret, instance subdomain and scope 'useraccount' to the Composio auth config. Composio then builds https://{subdomain}.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do and /oauth_token.do from the subdomain.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio. You should land on oauth_auth.do with response_type=code, log in, approve access, and come back with a code that Composio exchanges at oauth_token.do. Then make a REST call to confirm the token works. OAuth only works with REST APIs, not SOAP.

steps.title: Optionally narrow access with custom auth scopes
steps.detail: The 'useraccount' scope grants everything the user's roles allow. On Tokyo or later, an admin can create custom auth scopes and REST API Auth Scopes so the client can only reach specific REST APIs. If you do this, update the scope in Composio to match.

steps.title: Have each customer's admin register a client in their instance
steps.detail: For every customer instance, send the admin the steps above (Application Registry > New, Redirect URL = the Composio callback) and ask them to send back the Client ID, Client Secret and subdomain. ServiceNow has no central approval. The client exists only in that instance.
gotchas: If the instance uses SSO, the login redirects to the customer's IdP.

steps.title: (Optional) Set up client credentials for machine-to-machine access
steps.detail: If you want Composio's S2S_OAUTH2 mode instead of a per-user login, you need Washington DC or later. Set the system property glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled=true (Global scope), create a dedicated integration user with the needed roles, and register a client-credentials client linked to that user as the OAuth Application User.
gotchas: Known error: the Client Credentials form lists only the first 1000 users alphabetically when you pick the OAuth Application User.

steps.title: Plan for token refresh and rate limits
steps.detail: Refresh access tokens before they expire, based on expires_in (30 minutes by default). Prompt the user to re-authorize when the refresh token expires (100 days by default). Handle HTTP 429 responses, since each instance's Rate Limit Rules decide the limits.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit a scoped app for ServiceNow Store certification
steps.detail: Only needed if you want to distribute a scoped app through the ServiceNow Store. Certification covers platform integration, implementation security, performance and license reviews. OAuth access does not require it.

steps.title: Wait for Store certification
steps.detail: The certification team gives a timeline for each review. A third-party vendor reports 3-5 weeks from submission to approval. New versions may need to be recertified.

requirements.item: Admin role on the ServiceNow instance
requirements.detail: You need the admin role to create OAuth endpoints in System OAuth > Application Registry. A free PDI gives you admin access.

requirements.item: Redirect URL that exactly matches the Composio callback
requirements.detail: If it doesn't match, authorization fails with 'Invalid Redirect_URI'.

requirements.item: A per-instance OAuth client for each customer
requirements.detail: Each customer instance is its own authorization server, so its admin must create the client.

requirements.item: Washington DC or later, plus a system property, for client credentials
requirements.detail: Set glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled=true and link an OAuth Application User.

requirements.item: ServiceNow Store certification (only for Store listings)
requirements.detail: Covers platform integration, implementation security, performance and license reviews.

scopes.effect: This is the default and needs no review. It grants the full access of the authenticated user's roles, so the user's roles decide what the agent can do.

scopes.scope: Custom auth scopes / REST API Auth Scopes
scopes.effect: An instance admin defines these (Tokyo and later) to limit the client to specific REST APIs. They are not a public catalog, so the names vary by instance and must be set in the Composio config to match.

blockers.cause: The Redirect URL on the Application Registry record doesn't match the redirect_uri that Composio sends.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into the Redirect URL field and save.

blockers.symptom: No client credentials grant option in the Application Registry
blockers.cause: The instance is older than Washington DC, or the inbound client credentials property is not enabled.
blockers.fix: Set glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled=true in Global scope on Washington DC or later, or use the authorization code flow instead.

blockers.symptom: The integration user doesn't appear in the OAuth Application User picker
blockers.cause: Known error: the Client Credentials form in the New Inbound Integrations UI shows only the first 1000 users alphabetically.
blockers.fix: See ServiceNow KB2624687 for the workaround, for example by naming the integration user so it sorts early.

blockers.cause: The instance's Rate Limit Rules cap inbound REST requests per hour.
blockers.fix: Back off and retry, and ask the instance admin to adjust the rate limit rule for the integration user.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after about 100 days
blockers.cause: The refresh token expired (default lifespan 8640000 s).
blockers.fix: Have the user re-authorize, or ask the admin to raise the Refresh Token Lifespan on the client.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow because every customer instance is its own authorization server, so you always need your own client. For development, register one on a free PDI. For each customer, their instance admin creates a client in System OAuth > Application Registry with Composio's callback as the Redirect URL and shares the Client ID, Client Secret and subdomain. Composio also supports BASIC and S2S_OAUTH2 (client credentials) modes.

evidence.claim: Composio's ServiceNow toolkit has no managed OAuth. Its auth modes are OAUTH2, BASIC and S2S_OAUTH2, with templated per-instance oauth_auth.do and oauth_token.do URLs, default scope useraccount, and redirect https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.

open_questions: I couldn't fetch the current official docs for Zurich/Yokohama because they render with JavaScript. The form field labels come from community posts and may differ on newer releases.
It's unclear whether the Redirect URL field accepts multiple comma-separated URLs, and whether matching is exact or by prefix.
I couldn't confirm how PKCE is enabled on the registry record, or which release added it.
PDI terms (reclaim after inactivity, release upgrades) were not verified.
The live oauth_auth.do and OIDC discovery endpoints were not probed.
It's unconfirmed whether the 'useraccount' scope must be explicitly attached to the OAuth entity profile in newer releases for the authorization code flow to work with Composio.
